statement: For the polynomial $p(x) = -3x(x + 2)(x - 5)^2$, which of the following is the solution set of the inequality $p(x) \ge 0$?

choices.misconception: I made a sign chart for $x(x + 2)(x - 5)^2$ but forgot the leading factor of $-3$, so every sign I found was flipped.
I found where $-3x(x + 2)$ is positive or zero, but I forgot that $p(5) = 0$, so $x = 5$ also satisfies $p(x) \ge 0$.
I let the sign change at every zero, including $x = 5$, but the squared factor $(x - 5)^2$ is never negative, so the sign does not change there.

hints: The zeros $-2$, $0$ and $5$ split the number line into intervals. Find the sign of $p$ on each one, and remember that $\ge$ also allows $p(x) = 0$.
The factor $(x - 5)^2$ is positive except at $x = 5$, so away from $5$ the sign of $p$ is the sign of $-3x(x + 2)$.
$-3x(x + 2) \ge 0$ exactly when $x(x + 2) \le 0$, which is $-2 \le x \le 0$. Then check $x = 5$ on its own.

solutions.reliable: For $x \ne 5$, $(x - 5)^2 > 0$, so $p(x)$ has the same sign as $-3x(x + 2)$. That is positive or zero exactly when $x(x + 2) \le 0$, which happens for $-2 \le x \le 0$. At $x = 5$, $p(5) = 0$, which satisfies $p(x) \ge 0$. So the solution set is $-2 \le x \le 0$ or $x = 5$. Check with $x = -1$: $p(-1) = -3(-1)(1)(36) = 108 \ge 0$; with $x = 3$: $p(3) = -3(3)(5)(4) = -180 < 0$.
solutions.elegant: End behavior: the degree is $4$ and the leading coefficient is $-3$, so $p$ is negative far to the left and far to the right. The sign flips at the single zeros $-2$ and $0$, making $p$ positive between them, but not at the double zero $5$, where the graph only touches the axis from below. So $p(x) \ge 0$ on $-2 \le x \le 0$ and at the single point $x = 5$.
